A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOS for test-time adaptation of LiDAR-based 3D detectors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original adaptation experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies, and resource measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds component studies, retention and ensemble comparisons, another transfer task, and DSVT experiments.

M1.justification: Equations (1)-(12) and Algorithm 1 retain the same warm-up, similarity-weighted checkpoint assembly, pseudo-label training, and model-bank replacement procedures. The newly specified feature extraction details and additional evaluation backbones do not establish a change to MOS.

E1.justification: v2 adds Waymo-to-nuScenes adaptation in Appendix A.2 and Table 7, extending evaluation to nuScenes as the target domain. The existing KITTI-target tasks, object classes, and eight corruption types remain covered; no new dataset collection or corruption family is introduced.

E2.justification: Appendix A.1.4 and Table 6 add last-layer least squares and an adapted three-model bagging comparator for incomplete-echo corruption. The principal TTA and UDA comparisons are retained. The model-merging papers discussed in Appendix A.3 are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with a retrospective test on the first 32 point clouds, comparing the 32nd checkpoint against the final checkpoint bank using AP and Recall@0.5. It also introduces DSVT evaluation and frozen-encoder least-squares and random-update/NMS bagging protocols. Existing batch size 8, K=5, and L=112 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds incomplete-echo component ablations, rank-versus-cosine similarity and BEV-versus-RoI feature comparisons, an early-data retention study, and ensemble-alternative analyses in Appendix A.1. Backbone sensitivity testing expands from PV-RCNN to include DSVT. Existing hyperparameter studies, checkpoint visualizations, and resource analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, multiclass, corruption, component-ablation, and PV-RCNN values are retained. New result groups include Waymo-to-nuScenes AP3D of 18.75 for MOS versus 18.22 for MemCLR and 20.19 for ST3D, DSVT AP3D of 57.41 versus SAR's 37.45, and early-set AP3D of 14.04 for final checkpoints versus 4.14 for the 32nd checkpoint. These are added evaluations rather than improvements to retained results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, synergy-weight derivation, similarity equations, and bank-update equations remain unchanged. The complexity argument moves from Appendix A.5 to Section 4.4. New rank-similarity discussion supplies conceptual interpretation rather than a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain early exploration of TTA for 3D detection, checkpoint assembly using generalized-Gram synergy weights, and adaptation across dataset, corruption, and hybrid shifts. The headline 67.3% cross-corruption improvement and checkpoint-memory claim are retained; additional experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds substantive explanations concerning within-cloud diversity, environmental information in BEV features, and retention of early-scene knowledge. Appendices A.2-A.3 add interpretations of the nuScenes transfer difficulty and arguments about other ensemble methods' online applicability. Existing computational-cost and small-object limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the final-encoder BEV feature dimensions, the RoI alternative, and implementation details for the added ensemble comparisons. Existing hardware, augmentation, pseudo-labeling, and memory-management descriptions are retained. The direct MOS repository URL is replaced by a statement that code accompanies supplementary materials, whose availability cannot be verified from these PDFs.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 substantially expands positioning against checkpoint averaging, latest-weight averaging, Fisher-weighted merging, and model soups, citing Gao, Kaddour, Matena and Raffel, and Wortsman. Additional citations support bagging and DSVT. This extends the original domain-adaptation/TTA discussion to closely related ensemble research.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, consolidates the opening method subsections, moves complexity analysis into the main text, and reorganizes the appendix with a detailed roadmap. Author information, citation style, and wording also change, while most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a domain-shift overview figure and Tables 4-7, redraws the workflow, expands the backbone table, and moves the resource plot into the main text. The former Figure 5 ablation display becomes Table 3. Document styling and figure/table placement change throughout, while several existing displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added component, retention, ensemble, transfer, and backbone studies provide useful support beyond v1, and the ensemble discussion clarifies research positioning. The gain is limited by narrow settings for several new analyses and reporting weaknesses: Appendix A.1.1 calls 12.51 versus 16.14 a 29% reduction, although it is approximately 22.5%. Replacing the direct code URL also weakens access information. Overall, the additional evidence yields a modest net improvement.
